illustration.alt: Mary Childs records the Money Stuff podcast beside mortgage papers, auction paddles under a chandelier, IVV and VOO folders, and a note about missing Katie.

elementaryChecklist.financialMechanism: The episode discussed CDS payments after defined credit events, replacing mortgages through refinancing, and second-price auctions in which the highest bidder wins but pays the second-highest bid.
elementaryChecklist.centralJoke: A densely technical list of finance topics includes chandelier bidding and ends with the heartfelt conclusion that everyone misses Katie.

preschool.title: The Podcast with CDS, Chandeliers, and Katie
preschool.lesson: CDS can pay after contract-defined credit events, mortgage refinancing replaces an old mortgage with a new one, and a second-price auction charges the winner the second-highest bid.
paragraphs:
The Money Stuff microphones blinked on that day;
guest host Mary Childs had plenty to say.
From Mary in America, she came to discuss
a jumble of finance with sparkle and fuss.

There was gossip on CDS—contracts designed
to pay when defined credit trouble arrives.
Refinancing swaps an old mortgage for new;
“suboptimal” means it may not be best for you.

They weighed cheap options and savings-account rates,
hourly bills, AI, and apprentice debates.
Then came second-price auctions, with one clever twist:
the top bidder wins, paying second on the list.

Chandelier bidding swung into view,
then the IVV-to-VOO pipeline came through.
They compared rich-person trades with hedge-fund flair—
a remarkably crowded discussion to air.

Yet after each contract, each auction, each fee,
one point topped the agenda as plain as could be:
Whatever the trade, whatever its size,
they all missed Katie—no hedge could disguise.

On Apple or Spotify, listeners can press play;
other podcast services carry it today.
Bloomberg welcomed responses once listeners were through,
for thoughts on the episode and its financial stew.

What happened? Bloomberg released a Money Stuff podcast episode guest-hosted by Mary Childs, covering the listed financial topics and how much everyone misses Katie. The episode is available through Apple, Spotify, and other podcast services.
